realnvp_flow.interpretation: Structural validity passed for 1,000 generated samples with 32 features. Outputs are continuous log(count + uniform jitter), not integer counts or library-normalized expression; exact zeros and count likelihood cannot be inferred. Sample quality is mixed: feature Wasserstein discrepancy was 0.3185 versus a real-reference median of 0.0967 (3.29 times higher), failing its heuristic screen. Correlation discrepancy was close to the reference median, diversity distance ratio was 1.027, and the correlation, diversity, and overlap screens passed. No exact training duplicates were detected against the recorded reference subset. These passes do not establish biological usefulness or privacy, and the failed aggregate quality screen does not establish universal unusability. Training NLL declined while validation NLL increased recently, a pattern compatible with possible overfitting but not proof of its cause. This NLL describes fit to standardized continuous expression only. No downstream benefit was measured; the justified use is exploratory development and task-specific evaluation, with frozen final assessment still pending.
limitations: Quality screens are exploratory heuristics, not empirically calibrated guarantees of usability or biological benefit.
Quality comparisons used 405 matched samples; bootstrap intervals condition on one fitted model and do not capture training-seed variation.
The correlation discrepancy bootstrap interval [0.07583, 0.08644] excludes its reported point estimate of 0.05959; this discrepancy requires clarification before interpreting its uncertainty.
Overlap checks cover only the recorded training reference subset and provide no privacy guarantee.
Ten observed training epochs and descriptive validation trends cannot establish a causal training diagnosis or final-test performance.
Downstream utility was not evaluated, so expression similarity alone justifies no claim of biological or task benefit.
